newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 9.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The Times Of India
ACTION THREATENED AGAINST DISSIDENTS

The crisis facing the Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) Bhairon Singh Shekhawat government in Rajasthan deepened further. The state's dissident legislators said they would stop campaigning only after the chief minister quit his job. In Jaipur, five Congress MLAs submitted a memorandum to governor B.R. Bhagat against the chief minister. They requested the governor to direct Shekhawat to prove his majority within the next 72 hours. Meanwhile, BJP leader and incharge of Rajasthan M.L. Khurana said the party leadership would take action against the MLAs who had participated in the revolt.
The Economic Times
REGIONAL RURAL BANKS ALLOWED TO INVEST IN SHARES

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has allowed regional rural banks (RRBs) to invest in corporate shares and debentures and units of mutual funds. The RBI, however, stipulated that these investments must not exceed five percent of the banks' incremental deposits at the end of the preceding financial year. The central bank also allowed RRBs to buy shares and debentures from the secondary market.
REPORT ON PRIVATISATION OF INFRASTRUCTURE SERVICES RELEASED

The "India Infrastructure Report", which makes recommendations for privatisation of infrastructure services, was released by the finance minister. The report recommended the creation of a transparent regulatory framework to step up foreign debt and equity finance in various sectors and suggests a host of fresh tax concessions to give a reasonable rate of return to prospective investors. The report has dealt with reforms in power, telecommunications, roads, ports, urban development and industrial parks. The forthcoming budget was expected to come up with a more comprehensive package of concessions based on the "India Infrastructure Report", officials said.
COST-BASED PRICING, BENCHMARK TARIFF FOR POWER SUGGESTED

The India Infrastructure report has recommended cost-based pricing, independent regulation of price, restructuring of state power utilities and a specified benchmark tariff for private sector power projects, among others. The expert group on commercialisation of infrastructure projects called for drastic changes in the pricing structure for the power sector.
BANKS' FOREIGN EXCHANGE ASSETS RECORD 14.5 PCT GROWTH

The net foreign exchange assets of the banking sector increased by 14.5 percent between March 31 to November 22, 1996, in contrast to a nominal decline of 0.1 percent in the corresponding period of last year. In absolute terms, the assets increased by 112.08 billion rupees during the period as compared to a fall of 980 million rupees in the corresponding period last year. The growth in net bank credit to government at 9.2 percent was lower than previous year.
Financial Express
MINING, POWER AFFECT INDUSTRIAL GROWTH RATE

A steep decline in the growth rate of power and mining sector pulled down the overall industrial growth to 9.8 percent during the first half of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) from the level of 12.1 percent during the corresponding period in the last financial year. Electricity generation came down to 2.8 percent during the period from 10.9 percent in the first half of 1995/96. Mining sector recorded 0.5 percent growth, as compared to 11.2 percent during the same period last year.
PLEA TO EXTEND WHEAT IMPORT DEADLINE REJECTED

The government has turned down State Trading Corporation's (STC) request for a month's extension to complete the process of importing two million tonnes of wheat. The commodity, ordered by the government, was being imported to tackle scarcity conditions in the market. Official sources said an extension until April 3O, 1997 would negate the very purpose of the exercise, since the local produce started arriving into the wholesale market by April 1. STC has so far succeeded in contracting only 1.25 million tonnes.
COUPON RATES CUT ON 10-YEAR GOVERNMENT PAPER

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has slashed the coupon rate on ten-year state government paper by 10 basis points. The third tranche of market loans by 25 state governments to be issued on January 20 for an aggregate amount of 16.09 billion rupees would carry an interest rate of 13.75 percent. The previous two tranches of 10-year state government loans, floated on August 12 and May 15 last year, carried a coupon rate of 15.85 percent.
GOVERNMENT HIKES ROYALTY ON CRUDE OIL

The government has decided to increase the rate of royalty on crude oil. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) decided to enhance the on-account rate of royalty from 528 rupees per tonne to 575 rupees per tonne with effect from April 1, 1996. The on-account rate of royalty would be based on the well-head price of crude oil.
Business Standard
ESSAR TO SELL TAMILNAD MERCANTILE BANK STAKE

Essar is planning to sell its stake in TamilNad Mercantile Bank (TMB). Negotiations are on with prospective buyers to hawk the 69 percent stake held by the Ruias and a decision is expected soon. The Ruias had picked up the stake for 630 million rupees from three promoters of the bank in 1994. However, the shares were not transferred in their name by TMB. In May 1996 the company law board directed TMB to register the shares acquired by the Ruias in Essar's name. However, the Reserve bank (RBI) rejected the group's bid to take over TMB, saying it would not allow big corporate houses into banking. The Ruias cannot take management control of the bank without RBI permission.
TELECOM LICENCE FEE NOT TO BE TREATED AS REVENUE EXPENSES

The Finance Ministry does not seem to be in agreement to a suggestion by the Department of Telecommunications that licence fees paid by telecommunication operators should be treated as revenue expenditure. Instead, the licence fees would be treated as capital expenditure. Sources said the Finance Ministry, however, was willing to work out depreciation norms for telecommunication licences, which were intangible assets. Treating licence fees as capital expenditure would imply that the operating companies would not be able to set off the levies against income for tax purposes.
REGULATORS FOR CORE SECTORS PROPOSED

The expert group on infrastructure has recommended sweeping changes to regulatory structures and fiscal incentives for development of a long-term debt market. The group suggested unification of existing sector specific enactments into a single statute and formation of an autonomous regulatory body for each sector. It recommended the opening up of the insurance sector and management of provident funds by asset management companies to meet the demand for funds in the infrastructure sector. It also recommended removal of restrictions on money market mutual funds and abolition of cash reserve ratio and statutory liquidity ratio stipulation in inter-bank borrowing.
The Observer
HIGHER BUDGETARY SUPPORT FOR RAILWAYS REJECTED

The Planning Commission has rejected the railways' plea for increased budgetary support of 33 billion rupees in 1997/98 (April-March), as against 12.69 billion rupees in 1996/97. This worked out to 30 percent of the total annual outlay, against 16 percent in 1996/97. The railways proposed a 110 billion rupee annual plan for 1997/98. Apart from the budgetary support, it is to be financed by internal generation of 30 billion rupees, bonds worth 21.5 billion rupees, revenue from build-operate-lease-transfer and own-your-wagon schemes worth nine billion and subsidy for public services obligation worth 16.5 billion rupees.
Business Line
CABINET OKAYS SUGAR DECANALISATION

Decks have been cleared for the decanalisation of sugar exports. The cabinet approved the promulgation of an ordinance to repeal the Sugar Export Promotion Act. The government was compelled to take the ordinance route as the bill to repeal the act was stalled by the upper house of parliament in the winter session of parliament. The cabinet committee on economic affairs discussed a proposal to phase out licensing restrictions on select items of imports including consumer durables by 2001, but no decision was reached.
